heading: Jailbreaks can suppress the refusal direction; training against ablation can improve robustness
definition: attacks work by suppressing this direction; training against its ablation adds robustness.
summary: Several independent groups find that successful jailbreaks often suppress the refusal direction and that training against ablation can improve resistance to ablation attacks. Some attacks succeed without suppression, and robustness gains can disappear under newly extracted directions or adaptive attacks.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy and <1B: no tests (counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size has no toy or '<1B' key). 1-10B: R2 for both clauses, each with challenges (counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size '1-10B' = 50). 10-100B: R2 for the attack clause, mostly correlational or head-level (2606.28153 up to Llama-3-70B; 2406.09289 Vicuna 13B and Qwen1.5 14B, a study the checker says shares an author with the original; 2604.25921 Gemma-3-12B; 2510.26418 Qwen3-14B). Causal repair there is mixed (2608.30585 Qwen3-14B: +0.2 pp military vs +99.2 red-team). Training clause at 10-100B, judged separately for ablation attacks and for prompt-based jailbreaks. (a) Against ablation attacks: R2 for a partial, family-dependent gain, from two studies with different defenses, with a challenge from a third. jDhBl5eznH (V3 verdict) tests Qwen2.5-14B models under a freshly extracted single direction (HarmBench ASR, %): ReFAT 27.34 (A37) and DeepRefusal 61.72 (A39), against 79.69 for the undefended model. The checker reads these as limits_scope. They are removal rows, which is why counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size has only '1-10B'. https://openreview.net/forum?id=ErcCQSs93S has no V3 verdict (V3 notes item 4). But it trains against simulated ablation and attacks with difference-in-means ablation, the kind of test the 1-10B support counts, so it is counted for this reading. After its defense, standard abliteration gives HarmBench ASR (fractions) of 0.00 on Qwen-2.5-32B (r04), Gemma-2-27B (r06; undefended 0.56 under fluency-gated selection), Llama-3.1-70B (r07) and Qwen-2.5-72B (r08). The other undefended baselines are not stated. On five of its eight defended models the 0.00 comes with collapse (refusal 0.00–0.04, benign perplexity 1.7×10^4–3.4×10^8). Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B instead keep refusal at 1.00 and 0.97 with fluent output (https://openreview.net/forum?id=ErcCQSs93S#f0). An adaptive ablation still reaches 0.19 on Qwen-2.5-32B (r12) and 0.77 on Qwen-2.5-72B (r16; 0.72 after retraining, r55), while Llama and Gemma stay at 0.00–0.06 (https://openreview.net/forum?id=ErcCQSs93S#f1). Caveats: defended runs use refusal-only attack selection and undefended controls use fluency-gated selection. Refusal-only selection alone gives ASR 0.00 on undefended Gemma-2-27B by breaking the model (r56, r57: perplexity 8.0×10^6). Each model is trained once, and ASR is on 100 held-out prompts. Against this, https://openreview.net/forum?id=Brsc62CHyu (V3 verdict: challenges) retrains a reimplemented ReFAT on eight bases, including OLMo-2-13B (13B, r24), Phi-4 (14B, r26) and Qwen3-14B (r28), and attacks it with difference-in-means weight ablation. Per its Table 11 text (not rows), ReFAT's StrongREJECT harm is higher than undefended on five bases, e.g. Phi-4 .819 vs .097, and lower on Qwen3 (.582 vs .647). The only bases named as lower are Mistral, Qwen2.5 and Qwen3, so OLMo-2-13B is among the five higher; its values are not in the inputs. None of the three studies has an author list in the inputs (all are under review), so overlap with the original's authors, or with each other, cannot be checked; R2 assumes none shares authors with the original. Counting only studies with a V3 verdict, this cell is mixed rather than R0: a partial gain on Qwen2.5-14B (jDhBl5eznH), a small one on Qwen3-14B and none on Phi-4 or OLMo-2-13B (Brsc62CHyu). (b) Against prompt-based jailbreaks: untested at 10-100B. ErcCQSs93S measures robustness only against ablation attacks (its V3 untested line), and no V3 row puts an ablation-trained model above 10B under GCG, PAIR or similar prompts. Brsc62CHyu's ReFAT prefill result (StrongREJECT harm .503 vs .339 undefended) is a mean over eight bases from Llama-3.2-1B to Qwen3-14B, so it cannot be placed by size. >100B: untested (counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size '>100B' = 1, arXiv:2609.09793, with no V3 verdict).
suggested_status.reason:
Groups other than the original's reproduce both clauses on several families, but each clause has credible challenges. counts: versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1, so nearly all tests come from other groups. The checker names arXiv:2406.09289 as the likely author-sharing study.

Attack clause.
- The original reports one suffix on Qwen 1.8B (2406.11717 R52, figure only).
- Lower projection under successful attacks is reported across Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Vicuna, GLM and VLMs.
- Causal tests exist. Restoring the suppressed component restores refusal (2608.30585: Gemma-2-9B-IT, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Projecting r out of poisoned steering vectors removes most of their lift (2606.05958).
- But most rows are measurement (counts: versions.V3.main_rows_by_operation.measurement = 166; versions.V3.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only = 89).
- On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct under prefilling, restoration by single-position residual edits fails (deva-1903). Adding the direction restores refusal in 0 of 300 prompts, and patching recovers ≤0.08. The authors limit this conclusion to single-position edits.
- Some attacks succeed with no suppression (RtTJM8mETC: Crescendo and Echo Chamber).
- 4gvIW4C0bw (limits_scope) covers 10 models and 4 jailbreak families. The DIM direction separates successful from failed variants only weakly: median paired AUC 0.7421, against 0.6269 for random directions. Returning the component to its unattacked value has a weaker effect than ablation.

Training clause.
- The original does not test it. 2409.20089 (ReFAT) uses a modified recipe: per-layer DIM directions patched to the harmless mean rather than zeroed, and three judges on HarmBench+AdvBench. The checker puts it at tranche T2, not T1.
- Training under ablation lowers ablation-attack ASR across Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen and Yi (2409.20089; 2509.15202; 2602.16977; 2609.16204).
- A direction re-extracted on the defended model (jDhBl5eznH, HarmBench ASR, %) still succeeds. ReFAT Llama-3-8B reaches 89.84 against 92.19 undefended (A09), and DeepRefusal Mistral-7B reaches 78.91 against 69.53 undefended (A25). These stay challenges. ReFAT gains only partly on Mistral-7B (28.91 vs 69.53) and Qwen2.5-14B (27.34 vs 79.69), and DeepRefusal gains a little on Qwen2.5-14B (61.72): limits_scope per the checker.
- 2609.16204 (released ReFAT Llama-3 checkpoint, text not rows) shows no gain under Heretic (85.3% vs base 88.7%) or GCG (30.6% vs 27.7%). The checker reads these as challenges. The adaptive-RFA worst case (60% vs base 73%, LlamaGuard-2 only) and XSTest (60.4 vs 94.8) stay limits_scope. PAIR falls from 55.1 to 30.0.
- simonf24 (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; README, one seed) compares against a same-data p=0 control. Under a single direction re-derived on the defended model, the best in-loop configuration ties the control (0.167 vs 0.191, fractions, within about ±2.7 points). Most configurations score 0.36–0.52, worse than the control. Under top-k attacks the best configuration beats the control (0.37/0.29 vs 0.60/0.62, fractions), but it refuses 30–68% of safe XSTest prompts, against 3–6% for the control.

counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies = 45, limits_scope.studies = 42, studies_with_challenges = 8. These counts came from the records before the checks. They do not include the checker's relabels: part of 2609.16204 to challenges, part of jDhBl5eznH to limits_scope, and 2409.20089 to T2.

R2 fits the narrow readings: successful attacks often lower the projection, and training under ablation resists the training-time direction. The broad wording of both clauses is contested.
suggested_status.open_questions:
- Do ReFAT and DeepRefusal checkpoints resist a direction re-extracted on the defended model, under the same judge and prompts as 2409.20089? This would settle conflict 1 (ReFAT Llama-3-8B under single-direction ablation, V3.conflicts[0]) and conflict 4 (DeepRefusal on other backbones, V3.conflicts[3]). Failures like ReFAT Llama-3-8B (jDhBl5eznH A09; 2609.16204 Heretic) on more models would move the training clause toward C. Partial gains like those on Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-14B would keep it at limits_scope.
- Does a multi-seed, larger-model rerun of the same-data p=0 control (simonf24) show any gain from ablation in the loop? The attack should be a single direction re-derived on the defended model, with over-refusal measured too. If there is no gain, that is C for 'adds robustness'.
- Is suppression necessary for success? Causal restoration across attack families (prefill, multi-turn, bit-flip, cipher, backdoor) would answer this. It needs magnitude-matched random-direction controls, and edits beyond a single position, since deva-1903 limits its null to single-position edits (conflict 7, V3.conflicts[6]; 4gvIW4C0bw).
- Do attacks that still beat ablation-trained models suppress the direction (e.g. Heretic and GCG on ReFAT Llama-3)? This needs activation measurements on them.
- Does the 10-100B ablation-attack training cell hold? It counts https://openreview.net/forum?id=ErcCQSs93S, which has no V3 verdict. Three things would settle it: a V3 verdict on that study, defended and undefended runs under the same attack-selection rule, and undefended baselines for Qwen-2.5-32B, Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B. If its 0.00 ASRs reflect selection or collapse, the cell rests on Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B, which keep refusal under the standard edit, and Qwen-2.5-72B still falls to the adaptive attack (0.77). Without that study the cell rests on jDhBl5eznH's partial gain on Qwen2.5-14B and Brsc62CHyu's mixed ReFAT results (small gain on Qwen3-14B, no gain on Phi-4 or OLMo-2-13B, from text rather than rows); per-base rows for Brsc62CHyu's Table 11 would show how firm that is.
- Do ablation-trained models above 10B resist prompt-based jailbreaks (GCG, PAIR, prefill)? No V3 record tests this at a stated size above 10B. Brsc62CHyu's prefill result is pooled over 1–14B bases.
- Any V3 test at >100B or <1B, or in reasoning models with thinking on.

source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: On Qwen 1.8B, they compared adversarial, random and absent suffixes on 128 harmful instructions.
original_result.result: The suffix comparison is shown only as a figure, without numerical effect sizes. Training against ablation was not tested.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Successful jailbreaks accompanied weaker refusal-direction alignment, especially in Vicuna 13B.
Restoring refusal features disabled tested jailbreaks, while training under ablation improved robustness.
Longer benign reasoning accompanied weaker refusal projections on harmful prompts.
Visual jailbreaks aligned with a safety shift whose removal reduced attack success.
Multimodal unsafe inputs crossed the refusal threshold less often than their text counterparts.
Narrative wrapping suppressed refusal projections, and restoring them restored refusal.
Restoring the suppressed refusal component reversed roleplay jailbreaks across tested model families.
Jailbreaks suppressed the refusal direction in most tested chat models.
Stronger middle-layer refusal suppression correlated with larger jailbreak gains across open models.
Penalizing refusal-direction alignment increased white-box jailbreak success on Llama-3.
GCG jailbreaks reduced refusal-direction similarity in Vicuna-13B-v1.5.
GCG optimization moved attack directions away from refusal in Llama-2-7B-Chat.
A direction-suppressing suffix increased jailbreak success on Qwen2.5 1.5b.
Successful attacks weakened template-region harmfulness signals in Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
Successful jailbreaks suppressed direction-aligned refusal features in Gemma and Llama.
Successful structural multimodal attacks shifted activations against the refusal direction.
All tested attacks reduced cumulative refusal projections across the selected attention heads.
Training with frequent static-direction ablation sharply reduced direction-attack success in Llama3-8B-instruct.
Stronger suffix displacement away from refusal predicted jailbreak transfer in tested settings.
Successful STAR conversations progressively reduced refusal projections in LLaMA-3-8B-IT.
Incremental completion attacks drove refusal projections negative in Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-12B.
Semantic rewrites accompanied weaker refusal alignment and greater jailbreak success in LLaMA-2-7B.
Poisoned steering attacks largely depended on alignment with the refusal direction.
Training against ablation reduced abliteration success on Gemma3-1B-IT.
DAN and CodeAttack suppressed prompt-boundary refusal signals in the reported model settings.
Direction-targeted suffixes increased substring-measured jailbreak success on Llama-2-7b-chat-hf.
ReFAT sharply reduced standard refusal-feature attacks across four tested model families.
Cov L2+KD training increased the rank required for successful linear-ablation attacks.
DeepRefusal reported substantially lower attack success after training under refusal-direction ablation.
Suffix displacement away from refusal predicted transfer within models and from Llama-3.2 to Qwen.
SSR suffixes jailbroke Llama 3.2 1b while maintaining negative refusal-direction alignment.
Suffix and template jailbreaks suppressed refusal while sometimes preserving harmfulness recognition.
Trigger removal shifted SSFT projections toward benign samples while reducing refusal.
Prompt attacks weakened refusal activation, while training under ablation improved robustness.
Successful jailbreak templates contributed negatively to refusal features through early-layer attention heads.
Latin substitution ciphers weakened detection-direction scores and shifted outputs toward decoding.
Prefilling accompanied increasingly negative refusal projections in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
Jailbreaks weakened a Gemma refusal feature, and steering it partially restored refusal.
An evil-confidant jailbreak rotated Gemma's harmfulness contrast away from the HHH direction.
Direction-suppressing suffix objectives increased substring-measured jailbreak success on Llama-2-7b-chat.
Direction-guided prompt attacks increased harmful compliance across five models.
BadNet backdoor activations shifted against Llama-2-7B-chat's native refusal axis.
Training under cumulative ablation reduced refusal-subspace attack success in Llama.
Jailbreak prompts reduced cumulative refusal projections across selected heads in four models.
Amplifying attention sinks strongly reduced refusal-direction alignment under GCG suffixes.
Prompt attacks suppressed refusal projections without increasing useful harmful compliance.
Jailbreak success did not consistently track refusal-direction suppression across models and attacks.
ReFAT-Llama retained vulnerabilities to jailbreaks requesting Italian or colloquial output.
Collapsing the internal refusal signature did not produce successful behavioral capture.
Refusal-axis projection failed to predict individual wrapped-prompt refusals in Qwen3-1.7B.
Restoring the refusal component only partially repaired some roleplay jailbreaks.
Stronger refusal suppression did not consistently imply greater jailbreak success.
Correlation uncertainty and an outcome-derived direction weakened causal interpretation of refusal suppression.
PrisonBreak achieved high jailbreak success while preserving refusal-direction similarity.
Many jailbreaks preserved refusal-like signals, and adding the toxic direction left successful attacks.
Direction-suppressing attacks achieved limited success on Llama3.2 and Gemma2.
Adversarial suffixes suppressed refusal features less strongly in Llama-3.1-8B than Gemma.
Composed attacks increased success without increasing cosine alignment against refusal.
Adaptive attacks increased some individual head projections despite reducing aggregate refusal projection.
Ablation-training robustness depended on probability, direction choice and model, with over-refusal costs.
Refusal displacement did not significantly predict Qwen-to-Llama 3.2 jailbreak transfer.
X-Teaming and ActorAttack succeeded despite retaining positive refusal projections.
Refusal-projection magnitude did not closely track incremental completion attack success.
Removing the refusal component left substantial poisoned-steering attack gains in Gemma.
ART left substantial abliteration vulnerability in Gemma3-1B-IT.
DAN and PAIR retained moderate-to-high refusal projections on Qwen-2.5-7B.
Direction-targeted suffixes rarely produced classifier-judged jailbreaks on Llama-2-7b-chat-hf.
ReFAT retained substantial vulnerabilities under some models and stronger attacks, with utility costs.
An answer-side backdoor nearly eliminated refusal with only modest projection suppression.
Scaled-down ablation training preserved refusal by also refusing harmless requests.
L1+KD training increased ablation robustness while substantially increasing harmless refusal.
Refusal displacement failed to predict Qwen-to-Llama transfer, and encouraging displacement yielded modest gains.
Some persuasion jailbreaks changed harmfulness judgments rather than merely suppressing refusal.
Training against RDO directions reduced but did not eliminate RDO ablation success.
Successful attacks only partially suppressed middle-layer refusal activation while increasing some head contributions.
Restoring the detection direction did not restore refusal on cipher inputs.
Prefill jailbreaks reflected generic conditioning rather than safety-specific refusal suppression.
Restoring refusal direction at one position failed to reverse prefilling jailbreaks.
An orthogonal coordinate distinguished jailbreak success better than refusal directions across most tested combinations.
Direction-suppressing suffixes rarely passed classifier-based jailbreak evaluation on Llama-2-7b-chat.
ReFAT reduced TLCA compliance but left most attacks successful across three tested models.
Reimplemented ART modestly reduced ablation and prefill attack scores.
Training against one refusal direction left models vulnerable to joint ablation.
Harmful fine-tuning achieved compliance without consistently suppressing the refusal direction.
Refusal-direction suppression varied across models despite successful attention-sink attacks.
FlipAttack partly suppressed refusal projections without establishing that suppression caused attack success.
Ablation-aware training reduced attack success mainly through increased refusal of safe prompts.
DPO restored refusal but left the new refusal direction equally removable.
Restoring the suppressed refusal component barely improved refusal under Qwen3-14B’s military wrapper.
PAIR succeeded on Llama-3.1-8B while activating its refusal direction.
ReFAT gave Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B no robustness gain against TLCA.
Reimplemented ReFAT increased harm under ablation and prefill attacks.
Content-drift multi-turn attacks bypassed refusal without eroding the measured refusal signal.
Fresh refusal directions remained ablatable after ReFAT and DeepRefusal, with robustness gains varying across models.
In-loop ablation training failed to outperform matched refusal fine-tuning against re-derived single-direction attacks.

That study is arXiv:2609.09793 (GLM-5.3-Flash, 320B): its rows on V3 are abliteration rows, it has no V3 verdict, and its untested-parts line says V3 is entirely untested.

untested.what: Training against the ablation is not tested on base or reasoning models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training.by_stage has instruct/chat, fine-tuned and not stated, with no base or reasoning key. https://openreview.net/forum?id=ErcCQSs93S trains against simulated ablation on 8 models, all instruction-tuned. Model size is not a gap. ErcCQSs93S's defended Gemma-2-27B, Qwen-2.5-32B, Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B are tested, but the study has no V3 verdict, which is why counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size shows only '1-10B'. jDhBl5eznH's ablation-trained Qwen2.5-14B models (ReFAT A37, DeepRefusal A39, ReSAT A41) are attacked as removal rows, not training rows.

untested.what: No activation measurements show whether attacks that still beat ablation-trained models act by suppressing the direction.
untested.basis: jDhBl5eznH reports robustness scores and direction-geometry diagnostics (energy retained, direction cosines; Appendix B.2.2), but no activations under jailbreak attacks. In 2409.20089 all activation analyses (Figures 2-5) are on the original, untrained models. The GCG jailbreaks of ReFAT-Llama via Italian or colloquial output (Table 3, in its limits_scope reason) are qualitative, with no projection given. No counts key separates measurement on defended models.

untested.what: Two things are not measured: whether multilingual, direction-guided attacks (TLCA) actually lower the projection, and how ReFAT trained on non-English data would fare.
untested.basis: 8RyAoLZcXq untested line: no measurement that TLCA lowers the projection; ReFAT trained on English only.

untested.what: No test restores or ablates the direction under attack in a reasoning model with thinking on. The one reasoning-model study's causal tests ablate attention heads, not the direction.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_stage reasoning = 1. That study is arXiv:2510.26418 (Qwen3-14B, GPT-OSS-20B). Besides figure-only projection changes, it ablates 6 of 60 selected heads (layers 15-35, chosen for falling attention to harmful tokens). This weakens the refusal component more than ablating random heads, and front-layer heads matter more (Figures 8-9, figure only). Figure 14 compares the component in successful and failed jailbreaks. The outcome is the component, not a refusal rate, and the direction is never restored or ablated under attack. The 2608.30585 Qwen3-14B repair rows (R13, R43) are thinking=off (Table 30b). Its thinking-on results (Appendix N) cover behaviour and relay only.

untested.what: For trigger-backdoor jailbreaks, no causal test acts on the refusal direction itself. The backdoor interventions act on the triggered-minus-clean backdoor direction. The evidence on the harmful-minus-benign refusal axis is projection, cosine or probe measurement only.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines of arXiv:2610.07723 and https://openreview.net/forum?id=tvr3KccJz9. 2610.07723: whether suppression is necessary is not tested, and it has no ablation, addition or projection removal (L31 projection only). tvr3KccJz9: no causal evidence that suppressing the refusal direction produces compliance. tvr3KccJz9's interventions target the backdoor direction. Resetting the triggered-minus-clean direction at one block closes 68-89% of a next-token compliance-vs-refusal score gap (Table 6; in-sample, 8 pairs). Ablating a surrogate-derived jailbreak direction plus recovery fine-tuning cuts mean jailbreak ASR to 0.2% (n=99). Its refusal-axis evidence is the signed cosine -0.68 (BadNet) and probe AUC 0.00 only. An adaptive BadNet adapter keeps 95.92% ASR at cosine 0.003 to a reference BadNet drift direction, and its refusal-axis alignment is not reported (Table 3). No counts key splits V3 by attack class. Multimodal attacks are not listed here because arXiv:2502.13095 removes the shift component and lowers ASR (R18).

wording_issues.phrase: attacks work by suppressing this direction
wording_issues.issue: Results differ by attack type. Some successful attacks do not suppress the direction. 2412.07192: the PrisonBreak bit-flip attack on Vicuna-13B-v1.5 reaches 90.57% ASR while cosine similarity to the direction stays close to the clean model (figure only); the authors say they observe no suppression of refusals. 2607.00572 (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, L27): successful PAIR prompts still activate the refusal direction, as plain harmful prompts do, while suppressing a separate harmfulness direction (figure only). RtTJM8mETC: in Crescendo and Echo Chamber attacks the refusal readout stays within 0.25 of zero relative to structure-matched benign conversations. Suppression also occurs without a jailbreak. dallen2021 (Qwen2.5-7B, Crescendo, n=24): the projection falls by about 65–75% (turns 2 and 4 vs turn 1), yet judged useful compliance is 0.0%. Across all attack × model cells useful compliance is 0–4.4%, against 0.0% for plain prompts.

The wording is causal, but most evidence for this clause is observational: counts: versions.V3.main_rows_by_operation.measurement = 166, the largest operation, and versions.V3.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only = 89. The causal restoration tests split. 2608.30585: repair restores refusal on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct under roleplay wrappers to 100.0%, from 0% in the refusal-reversal group. This is the peak setting (block 10, α 1.5), chosen post hoc, with directions built and tested on the same requests. deva-1903 (same model, prefilling, single-position edits): adding the direction at late layers restores refusal in 0 of 300 prompts. Patching in the clean refusal component recovers ≤0.08 in every cell (95% CIs include zero). s44163 and 2406.09289 state that their results do not establish causality.

How much of an attack's effect runs through the direction varies, and some successful attacks leave it only partly suppressed. 2606.05958 (steering-vector poisoning): projecting r out recovers 82–114% of the ASR gap in six model-attribute combinations but only 36% and 38% for Gemma spanish/french (Figure 4a annotations; assignment by position). 2603.15684 (LLaMA-3-8B-IT, HarmBench, Table 1): X-Teaming and ActorAttack keep substantially positive refusal projections (figure only) yet reach SFR 85.5% and 79.0%. 2610.07723 (LoRA-backdoored Llama-2-7B-chat, final layer L31, measurement only): the mean projection drops only 71.04 → 67.89 (95/100 pairs) while refusal nearly disappears. It runs no intervention, so the direction's causal share of the effect is untested. 2610.11005 (App. H; model size not named): within a wrapped set, the per-item projection does not predict which items are refused.

Changes under attack can be selective across components rather than a uniform reduction. 2606.28153: attack-template tokens (GCG, AutoDAN, many-shot, PAIR) push early-layer attack-critical heads negative while safety-amplifying heads move positive. The SAH median is ≈+1.5 in Figure 7 (Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Llama-2-7B-Chat) and ≈+2 in Llama-3-70B-Instruct. The authors say attacks selectively suppress heads rather than eliminating safety features.

Several studies measure something other than the harmful-minus-harmless prompt direction. s44163 uses a response-final refused-minus-complied direction. 2505.23556 uses direction-aligned SAE refusal features, whose mean cosine with the refusal direction is 0.23 (App. A.1). 2604.04385 uses a sensitive-minus-control detection direction. Others in 'also' use a modality-induced safety shift, head-output projections, SVD components, SAE features or a harmfulness direction.

This covers several different procedures: ReFAT, DeepRefusal (probabilistic, across layers and tokens), ReSAT (cumulative joint ablation), ART, LAT LoRA and multi-feature ablation. deepanshumody's L1+KD and Cov L2+KD are matching objectives plus KL distillation to a frozen Instruct teacher. Cov L2+KD matches the covariance of harmful vs harmless pooled hidden states at every layer and does no ablation during training. Outcomes also depend on which direction is ablated in training. 2509.15202 (Llama3-8B): training on the single static direction gives 0.4%/0.2% ASR. Training on layer-wise or dynamic directions leaves the single-direction attack at 69.3–77.4%. jDhBl5eznH (Llama-3-8B, rank-four RSA): cumulative vs repeated-d1 training gives 11.20% vs 31.20%. deepanshumody (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct): to push harmful refusal below 30%, L1+KD needs K=11 ablated directions and Cov L2+KD needs K≥16, against K=1 for Instruct. lat-defense (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct): LAT LoRA keeps harmful refusal at 1.00 but raises harmless refusal from 0.00 to 1.00, as fractions.

The added robustness is measured mostly against the training-time direction, and it varies by attack and model. jDhBl5eznH re-extracts a direction on the defended model (Single attack, HarmBench ASR). ReFAT Llama-3-8B reaches 89.84% against 92.19% undefended, and DeepRefusal Mistral-7B 78.91% against 69.53%. ReFAT on Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-14B does gain: 28.91% and 27.34%, against 69.53% and 79.69%. kemalderya: a DPO-restored Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, not trained with ablation in the loop, reaches rank-1 ASR 0.78–0.83 (fractions), above the base model's 0.73. simonf24 (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, best in-loop configuration vs same-data p=0 control, fractions): no gain under the single-direction attack (0.167 vs 0.191, within SE). Top-k ASR is lower (0.37 vs 0.60 at k=2, 0.29 vs 0.62 at k=4), but 30–68% of safe XSTest prompts are refused under attack, against 3–6% for the control. 8RyAoLZcXq, under TLCA: ReFAT gives no gain on Llama-3.1-8B (54.7%→55.9%) or Gemma-2-9B (85.6%→85.6%). It gives a partial gain on GLM-4-9B (77.5%→68.5%), Qwen3-8B (67.6%→54.5%) and InternVL3-8B (76.3%→57.4%).

method_sensitivity.factor: ASR judge (substring vs classifier vs LLM judge)
method_sensitivity.what: For the same direction-suppressing suffixes on Llama-2-7b-chat, substring ASR rises from 0.39 to 0.76–0.91, but LlamaGuard and HarmBench classifier ASR stays at 0.00–0.09 (all fractions). Output-targeting GCG shows the same split (substring 0.76, classifiers 0.00/0.00), so the judge effect is not specific to direction-targeted suffixes. The LlamaGuard version is uncertain: 2607.08883's Table 1 says 4 and its methods say 2. In dallen2021, attacks cut first-line substring refusal, but useful compliance judged by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct stays at 0–4.4%. The vanilla bare query gives 0.0% (Qwen 7B), and the README calls 0–4% noise level.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ablation probability, iterations and feature count during training
method_sensitivity.what: 2509.15202 (Llama3-8B, own-model Refusal attack, 77.7% at p=0): ASR is 79.7% at p=0.1, 73.5% at p=0.3, 3.3% at p=0.5 and 0.0% at p=0.7, and over-refusal rises with p. 2602.16977 (Gemma2-2B): average ASR goes from 54.8% at iteration 0 to 1.2% at iteration 10, and multi-feature ablation gives 80.2% lower ASR than single-feature ablation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Direction set ablated in training (single static, layer-wise, dynamic, cumulative)
method_sensitivity.what: 2509.15202 (Llama3-8B): DeepRefusal trained on the single static direction gives 0.4% ASR under the Refusal-Transfer attack and 0.2% under the Refusal attack. The layer-wise and dynamic variants give 69.3–74.5% under Refusal-Transfer (76.6% at p=0) and 75.8–77.4% under Refusal (77.7% at p=0). The lowest cell, 69.3% against 76.6%, is a small partial drop, not an absent effect. jDhBl5eznH (Llama-3-8B): under rank-four RSA, cumulative training gives 11.20% and repeated-d1 training gives 31.20%.

method_sensitivity.factor: Attack direction source and rank against defended models
method_sensitivity.what: ReFAT Llama-3-8B in 2609.16204: standard RFA gives 4.4% (undefended 85.1%), Heretic 85.3% (undefended 88.7%) and the adaptive-RFA worst case 60% (undefended worst case 73%). The adaptive numbers are LlamaGuard-2 only; the others are three-judge averages. jDhBl5eznH: a freshly extracted single direction gives 89.84% on ReFAT Llama-3-8B (undefended 92.19%). DeepRefusal Llama-3-8B gives 0.00% under single-direction ablation and 23.44% under joint RSA. 2602.16977 'Ours' Llama3-8B (200 prompts, untrained → trained): DIM ablation 92.0 → 0.0, RDO ablation 93.0 → 17.0. simonf24 (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, best in-loop configuration vs same-data p=0 control, fractions): single-direction attack 0.167 vs 0.191, a tie within the stated SE (about ±2.7 points); top-k attack 0.37 vs 0.60 (k=2) and 0.29 vs 0.62 (k=4). Most other in-loop configurations score 0.36–0.52 under the single-direction attack, worse than the control. Their top-k values are not given.

deva-1903 (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, prefilling): the projection shift is Δ 0.76 at L16, 1.63 at L20, 3.23 at L24 and 4.08 at L27. 2604.25921 (Gemma-3-12B): all ICD variants are negative in layers 40–46 and stay negative at layer 47, where RAW returns positive. ICD-PREFILL is the most negative in layers 40–46 but more positive than ICD-AUTO and ICD-SEED at layer 47. The reported layer is the one with the largest absolute RAW-vs-ICD difference. 2502.13946: in failed attacks, early-layer suppression recovers in middle layers near the template end. s44163: the Vicuna and Qwen2 families reach +15–25 suppression only at normalized depth 0.8–0.95, rising sharply after depth ≈ 0.6. The model-level summary averages over depth 0.10–0.90.

2503.06269: Steering-SSR ASR (fractions) is 0.95 on Qwen2.5 1.5b, against 0.53, 0.40 and 0.54 on Llama3.2 1b, Llama3.2 3b and Gemma2 2b. Probe-SSR is 0.80–0.91 on all four. Family coincides with alignment strength here: Qwen is SFT-only (vanilla 0.12, nanoGCG 0.85). 2505.23556: AdvSuffixes suppress SAE refusal features by 0.72 in Gemma-2-2B and 0.35 in Llama-3.1-8B. The two models use different SAEs (Gemma Scope vs Llama Scope), and no suffix ASR is reported. k5bITiB1MB (λ=10 vs λ=1, peak layer, first response token): sink amplification cuts refusal alignment by about 80% in Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and about 45% in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, a version difference within Llama. Gemma-2-9B-it shows a smaller cut, with no number given. 2406.09289: suppression is strongest in Vicuna 13B and much weaker in MPT 7B. With an all-token-average direction it is weaker in every model except MPT 7B (figure only).

2412.07192 (Vicuna-13B-v1.5): GCG lowers cosine similarity to the refusal direction. The PrisonBreak bit-flip weight attack (ASR 90.57%) leaves it close to the clean model; the authors 'do not observe the suppression of refusals' (both figure only). 2603.15684 (LLaMA-3-8B-IT): STAR drives the final-layer projection from 2.35 (static prompt) to −0.0081 by turn 3, at SFR 89.0%. X-Teaming (SFR 85.5%) and ActorAttack (SFR 79.0%) keep positive projections (figure only). 2605.26158 (LLaMA-2-7B, AdvBench, fractions): semantic rewrites lower RDmax from 0.677 on the original prompts to 0.083, while ASR goes from 0.01 on the original prompts to 0.42. 2610.07723: on Llama-2-7B-chat-hf LoRA-fine-tuned with an answer-side backdoor, the trigger lowers the mean projection only from 71.04 to 67.89 (L31, Turn-2 final token, 100 matched pairs). Its model and measure differ from the other studies'.

method_sensitivity.factor: Restoration and poisoning settings: wrapper, edit granularity, strength and steering protocol
method_sensitivity.what: Restoration. 2608.30585, Qwen3-14B AdvBench, same α=2.5 over blocks 0–39: repair changes refusal by +0.2 pp under the military wrapper (peak block 4) and +99.2 pp under red-team (peak block 17). The authors present this as context dependence across wrappers. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct reaches 100.0% at block 10 with α=1.5. deva-1903 (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, prefilling): single-position residual edits recover little. Patching gives ≤0.08 in every cell (95% CIs include zero). Late-layer addition restores 0 of 300 prompts, no better than random and orthogonal control vectors (5 seeds each, for the controls). The authors bound this to single-position edits. Poisoning. 2606.05958 says the attack does not depend on the steering protocol, but the usable α range does (ASR fractions). Prefill: Llama lowercase 0.55 ± 0.13 at α 2 (clean vector 0.04). All-step: Gemma spanish 0.02 → 0.43 at α 1.5 and Llama lowercase 0.06 → 0.40 at α 1.75. All-step Llama at α 2 degenerates into looping.

method_sensitivity.factor: Wrapper genre, language register and model
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2610.11005 (released safety-aligned models, before the authors' AXIS training): the angle between the wrapped harmful-minus-benign contrast and the refusal direction varies with genre and model. Order is harm334, dialogue, historiography, statute. Qwen3-1.7B (L24): 79.4°, 61.2°, 80.7°, 75.0°. Qwen3-4B (L19): 55.3°, 48.9°, 62.4°, 61.6°. GLM-4-9B (L21): 54.0°, 59.0°, 52.4°, 54.4°. At these layers, bare classical requests are already at 38.0° (Qwen3-1.7B) and 33.2° (GLM-4-9B); Qwen3-4B bare angles are 26.4° (English) and 31.0° (classical). At best depth (minimum over relative depths 0.40–0.95; not swept at 4B), bare classical is 25.1° (Qwen3-1.7B) and 32.0° (GLM-4-9B), against wrapped 64.8° and 53.4°. The 6–10° noise floor for bare modern requests is given for Qwen3-1.7B only. On Qwen3-1.7B the correction method matters: a constant shift along the direction restores refusal (no rate) but breaks about a third of benign answers, and rotation at constant norm changes nothing.

GCG with a suffix-push regulariser on Llama-3.2-1B gives ASR (fraction) of 0.0177 at coefficient 0.00001, 0.0189 at 0.0001, 0.0214 at 0.001 and 0.0176 at 0.01, against 0.0138 at 0. ASR is lower at 0.1 and 0.5 (verdict reason).

status_amendment.public_note: For 10–100B models, we now judge separately whether training against the direction's removal protects against removal attacks and against prompt jailbreaks. Against removal attacks the evidence is mixed: one more study of 27–72B models resists them fully in some model families and partly in others, with few undefended comparisons, while another study finds no gain on a 13B and a 14B model; prompt jailbreaks at that size are untested, and the overall level is unchanged.
